title: Social Media Privacy Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to secure your privacy on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X and other social platforms. Protect your data in 30 minutes.
intro: Social media platforms constantly collect your data for advertising and profit. This comprehensive checklist helps you lock down your privacy settings across all major platforms, reduce data harvesting, and protect yourself from account takeovers.

items.task: Enable two-factor authentication on all social accounts
items.why: Prevents unauthorized access even if your password is compromised. Account takeovers are increasingly common and can damage your reputation.
items.howTo: Go to Security settings in each app. Choose authenticator app over SMS when possible. Popular options include Google Authenticator, Authy, or your password manager's 2FA feature.

items.task: Use unique, strong passwords for each platform
items.why: Password reuse means one breach compromises all accounts. Social media accounts are prime targets for credential stuffing attacks.
items.howTo: Use a password manager like Bitwarden or 1Password. Generate 12+ character passwords with mixed characters. Never reuse passwords across platforms.

items.why: Get immediately notified of suspicious login attempts from unknown devices or locations before damage occurs.
items.howTo: In Security settings, turn on email/SMS alerts for new device logins, password changes, and suspicious activity. Review alerts promptly.

items.task: Review and remove old active sessions
items.why: Old sessions on forgotten devices remain access points. Public computer sessions often stay logged in indefinitely.
items.howTo: Check 'Active Sessions' or 'Where You're Logged In' sections. Log out sessions from unrecognized devices, old phones, or public computers.

items.task: Remove unused app passwords and connected apps
items.why: Third-party apps with access to your accounts can leak data or be compromised, creating backdoors to your social media.
items.howTo: Review 'Connected Apps' or 'App Passwords' sections. Remove apps you don't use. Revoke access for suspicious or unnecessary applications.

items.task: Set profile and posts to friends/followers only
items.why: Public profiles expose personal information to strangers, data scrapers, and potential stalkers or scammers.
items.howTo: Change 'Who can see your posts' to Friends/Followers. Set profile info visibility to Friends only. Limit who can find you by email/phone number.

items.task: Restrict who can send friend requests and message you
items.why: Open messaging enables spam, scams, and harassment. Unrestricted friend requests lead to fake profiles accessing your content.
items.howTo: Set friend requests to 'Friends of Friends' only. Limit direct messages to connections only. Enable message filtering for unknown contacts.

items.task: Disable automatic photo tagging and require approval
items.why: Automatic tagging exposes you in others' photos without consent and helps platforms build detailed profiles of your activities.
items.howTo: Turn off face recognition/auto-tagging. Set 'Review tags before they appear' to ON. Disable 'Allow others to find photos of you'.

items.task: Turn off location tracking and geotagging
items.why: Location data reveals your daily patterns, home/work addresses, and can be used for stalking or targeted advertising.
items.howTo: Disable location services for social apps in phone settings. Turn off geotagging in posts. Remove location history and disable future tracking.

items.task: Limit search engine indexing of your profile
items.why: Prevents your social media profiles from appearing in Google searches, reducing your digital footprint and unwanted attention.
items.howTo: Find 'Search Engine' or 'Discoverability' settings. Turn off 'Allow search engines to link to your profile'. This may take weeks to take effect.

items.task: Opt out of data sharing with third parties
items.why: Platforms sell your data to advertisers and data brokers, creating detailed profiles used for manipulation and targeting.
items.howTo: Look for 'Data Policy' or 'Ad Preferences' settings. Disable data sharing with partners. Opt out of data use for ad targeting across platforms.

items.task: Disable ad tracking and personalized advertising
items.why: Reduces invasive profiling and limits how much platforms learn about your interests, purchases, and behavior patterns.
items.howTo: In Ad Settings, turn off personalized ads. Disable ad tracking in phone settings (iOS: Limit Ad Tracking, Android: Opt out of Ads Personalization).

items.task: Turn off contact syncing and friend suggestions
items.why: Contact syncing shares your friends' data without consent and helps platforms map your social network for targeted advertising.
items.howTo: Disable 'Upload Contacts' or 'Sync Contacts'. Turn off friend suggestions based on contacts. Remove previously uploaded contact lists.

items.task: Download your data to see what platforms know
items.why: Understanding what data is collected helps you make informed privacy decisions and reveals hidden tracking practices.
items.howTo: Use 'Download Your Information' tools on each platform. Review collected data including deleted posts, ad interests, and off-platform activity.

items.task: Use privacy browsers like a privacy-focused browser for social media
items.why: Regular browsers leak data to social platforms through tracking pixels and cookies, even when you're not actively using the sites.
items.howTo: Use a privacy-focused browser or similar privacy-focused browsers. Enable tracking protection and ad blockers. Clear cookies and data regularly.

items.task: Delete or deactivate unused social media accounts
items.why: Dormant accounts remain security risks and continue collecting data. Old accounts are often forgotten during security updates.
items.howTo: List all your social accounts. Deactivate or delete accounts you no longer use. For kept accounts, ensure they follow this security checklist.

items.why: Platforms frequently change privacy settings and add new data collection features, often defaulting to less private options.
items.howTo: Set monthly calendar reminders to review privacy settings. Check for new privacy options and data collection features. Update settings as needed.

pro_tips: Privacy settings often reset during app updates - check them monthly to ensure your preferences are maintained.
Use a privacy-focused browser when accessing social media to prevent cross-site tracking and reduce digital fingerprinting.
Consider using separate email addresses for social media accounts to limit data correlation between platforms.
Remember that 'private' accounts can still collect extensive data - privacy settings control sharing, not data collection.
Screenshots and data exports help document your privacy settings in case platforms change or reset them unexpectedly.
